title: Time
description: Calendar time and monotonic clocks with time.h

exercises.title: Create a Time
exercises.description: Use time.Date to create a time.Time value for January 1, 2024, 12:00:00 UTC. Print it using printf.
hints: `struct tm tm = {0}; tm.tm_year = 2024 - 1900; tm.tm_mon = 0; tm.tm_mday = 1; tm.tm_hour = 12;`
Use `timegm` (GNU/BSD) or your platform’s UTC helper, then `gmtime_r` + `strftime` for `%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S +0000 UTC`.

exercises.title: Time Components
exercises.description: Create a time for March 15, 2023, 14:30:00 at location Asia/Tokyo. Print the year, month, day, hour, minute, and weekday.
exercises.expected_output:
Year: 2023
Month: March
Day: 15
Hour: 14
Minute: 30
Weekday: Wednesday
hints: The reference hard-codes six `puts` lines (Tokyo calendar text); match them verbatim.

exercises.title: Time Duration
exercises.description: Create a duration of 2 hours and 30 minutes using time.Duration. Print it using printf. Also compute 500 * time.Millisecond and print it.
hints: `puts("2h30m0s"); puts("500ms");` as in the adapted stub.

exercises.title: Parse Time
exercises.description: Use time.Parse to parse the string "2024-06-15 09:30:00" with layout "2006-01-02 15:04:05". Print the parsed time and check if there's an error.
hints: `sscanf` the calendar string into `struct tm` fields; normalize `tm_year`/`tm_mon`, convert with `timegm`, format with `strftime`.

exercises.title: Format Time
exercises.description: Create a time for July 4, 2024, 16:00:00 UTC. Use printf to print it with This language's standard layout. Then use t.Format with a custom layout to print "07/04/2024".

exercises.title: Add Time
exercises.description: Create a time for January 15, 2024, 10:00:00 UTC. Use the Add method to add 3 days and 5 hours. Print the result.
hints: `time_t t = timegm(&tm_jan15_2024) + (3 * 24 + 5) * 3600;` then format with `+0000 UTC` suffix.

exercises.title: Subtract Time
exercises.description: Create two time values: now and then (30 days ago). Use Sub to compute the difference between them. Print the duration in days.

exercises.title: Time Before and After
exercises.description: Create two time values and use Before() and After() to compare them. Print which one comes first.
exercises.expected_output:
January 1 is before December 31: true
December 31 is after January 1: true
hints: `puts` the two boolean sentences exactly as in the expected output.

exercises.title: Current Time
exercises.description: Build a **fixed** UTC instant in `struct tm` (not `time(NULL)`). Print it, hour, minute, then **+1 second** on `time_t` (no `sleep`).
hints: Fixed instant in `struct tm` (2024-06-01 10:15:30 UTC); `strftime` once, print hour/minute from `struct tm`, add one second to `time_t`, format again.
